region: Hammondsport · Keuka Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Célèbre comes from Dr. Konstantin Frank, the Keuka Lake winery that changed the course of East Coast wine. Frank, a Ukrainian-born viticulturist with a doctorate from Odessa, arrived in New York in 1951 and insisted, against the opinion of the day, that European vinifera vines could survive Finger Lakes winters. He bought land on Keuka Lake’s west shore near Hammondsport in 1958 and founded his winery in 1962. The family still runs it: his grandson Fred Frank has led the estate since 1993, and a fourth generation has joined.

In 1980 Konstantin’s son Willy bought a historic cellar nearby to make the Finger Lakes’ first méthode champenoise sparkling wine, and it remains the home of the family’s sparkling program. Célèbre is made entirely from Riesling grown on Keuka estate plots that Willy planted for sparkling wine in the early 1980s. The grapes are hand-picked and pressed as whole clusters, and only the first, gentlest pressing is used. After its second fermentation in bottle the wine rests at least two years on its lees; each bottle is then disgorged, corked and labeled by hand, with the disgorgement month printed on the back.

Finished semi-dry, with about 20 grams per liter of residual sugar, Célèbre is the softer, fruit-forward member of the family’s sparkling range. The winery describes aromas of apple, honey and spice carried by Riesling’s firm acidity, which keeps the sweetness in balance. It suggests oysters, lobster, smoked salmon, sushi and fried foods alongside it, and, with a wink, popcorn.
facts: Méthode champenoise; whole-cluster pressed, first pressing (cuvée) only
At least 24 months on the lees; hand-disgorged
